pluginText.pf.license: {"need":"Electrical work in a home needs a license where the state, city or county licenses electricians. Some states license by job size or kind of work, like residential-only or limited licenses.","who holds it":"Both: the company (an electrical contractor license, where the state asks) and each electrician (apprentice, journeyman or master, where the state licenses people).","what to ask":["The company's license number and class","Each electrician's own number and level, in their invite reply","The local license for the job's city or county, where only cities or counties license home electrical work","Any specialty license and its limits, like low voltage, solar or signs: from the state form"],"how it's checked":"none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie","blocks going live":"The company's electrical listing goes live once it's set up. Each electrician is offered only once the owner says yes.","job limits":"Where a license stops at a job size or a kind of work, each quote and extra job is checked against it before it's sent.","renewals":"Reminders before each expiry, on the dates the owner picks (the example: 5 weeks and 1 week before). A lapsed license pauses new bookings for that person.","insurance or bond":"Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one: from the state form.","background checks":"Only where the state's form asks.","lead-safe work":"Cutting into painted walls or ceilings in an older home: a lead-safe certified firm and worker, where the rules require it.","at the counter":"Lamps and fixtures brought to the shop counter are cord-and-plug work, not wiring in a building: the state's form says if it needs a license. Safe default: the company's license on file, shown on the listing.","local rules":"The business's own word, never checked by Rosie (MC:C7)."}

pluginText.pf.safety: {"stops the booking":[{"words":"Smoke, sparks, a burning smell, or a hot panel, outlet or switch","says":"Get everyone out, and don't touch the panel. Call 911 from outside.","booking":"No booking until the fire department says the home is safe. The customer can come back then."},{"words":"A downed or sparking power line","says":"Stay at least 30 feet away, and keep others away. Call the power company's emergency line, or 911 if it's sparking or anyone is hurt.","booking":"No booking now. Damage on the house's side, like the meter box or the pipe the wires come in through, is booked once the power company makes it safe."},{"words":"Someone got a shock or is hurt","says":"Don't touch them if they may still be touching power. Call 911.","booking":"No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back."},{"words":"A gas smell","says":"Leave the house now. Then call 911 and the gas company.","booking":"No booking."}],"safety steps, then the booking goes on, marked urgent":[{"words":"Water near outlets, a light or the panel","says":"Stay away from the water and anything plugged in. Don't touch a switch or the panel while standing in water. Switch off that breaker only from a dry spot."},{"words":"A breaker that won't reset, or power out in part of the home","says":"Don't keep resetting it. Unplug what's on that circuit. If you smell burning, get out and call 911."},{"words":"A lamp or cord that sparked (at the counter)","says":"Unplug it and don't use it. Bring it in, or book a home visit if it's wired into the house."}],"a fix the customer declines":"A hazard left as it is: the circuit is switched off and labeled, and the customer gets a written safety note not to use it. The note stays with the job.","at the counter":"A light that's still wired into the house isn't worked on at the counter. Taking it down or putting it up is a home visit.","general screen":"Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first."}

pluginText.pf.visit: {"check-in at the customer's place":"The check-in code at the door. The on-my-way text names the electrician, with a photo.","check-in at the counter":"The code at the counter (the lamp tech or the desk types it). pluginText.pf.money: {"starting answers":["At the customer's place: a card saved for the $89 service call fee, and Rosie texts the bill after the job","An owner may take nothing before, or save a card only, with no hold (the old example took nothing before)","At the counter: nothing held; a card saved for the $20 fee; paid at the counter. Insurance: the customer pays, and gets the receipt and photos for the claim.","tips":"Off by default.","tax":"No tax line unless the owner sets a rate where the state taxes the work.","parts":"Parts at cost or at list, the owner's pick; permit fees on the quote; parts billed after go on the bill.","Rosfield's $2":"Applies, as for every kind of work."}
pluginText.pf.messages: {"never in a text":"Gate or lock codes, card details, and photos from inside the home or of the panel: these stay on the secure page.","languages":"English and Spanish.","danger words":"Fire, smoke and power line words always get the safety message first, before anything else."}
pluginText.pf.staff: {"levels":"Apprentice (or trainee), journeyman and master; each person's own license per state, where the state licenses electricians.","skills":["Outlets and switches","Breakers and circuits","Lights and fans","Panels and service changes","EV chargers","Generators","Safety inspections","Solar (its own license where the state asks)","Counter: lamps and fixtures","Counter: antique lamps"],"supervision":"An apprentice works only with a journeyman or master on the job, where the state's rules require it. pluginText.pf.rules: {"written contract":"A signed written contract before work above an amount, and no money before it's signed: from the state form.","right to cancel":"A written right to cancel for work sold at the home: where the rules require it.","permits":"Pulled by the license holder where the local rules require one; the inspection follows.","power company":"The power company's shut-off and turn-on for a panel swap or a service change.","lead-safe work":"Lead-safe work rules for older homes: where the rules require it.","license on papers":"The license number on listings, confirmations, quotes and bills: from the state form.","one service charge":"One service charge per visit, shown before the customer agrees: where the state's rules require it.","old parts":"Offer the customer the replaced parts: where the state's rules require it.","digging":"A utility locate before any digging: always.","declared emergency":"Price limits in a declared emergency: where the state's rules require it.","warranty":"The owner's own (the example: 1 year on labor), shown on the receipt.","records":"7 years, as for every kind of work."}
pluginText.pf.edges: {"all":"Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for electrical work:","electrical":["Smoke, sparks or a burning smell at any point: stop, get everyone out, call 911","A downed power line: 30 feet away, and call the power company","The problem gets worse before the visit: the safety steps again, then urgent","After hours: sent now to the electrician on call, then the backup; nobody takes it means no visit tonight and the hold released","A fix for a hazard declined: the circuit left off and labeled, with a written safety note","A bigger job found, like a scorched panel: its own quote, OK'd by the owner over the limit, with its permit","A panel swap: the permit, the power company's shut-off and turn-on, and the inspection before the last stage is billed","A quote past what the license allows: not sent, and the owner is told","Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee","A renter whose landlord pays: the landlord's OK first, or the renter pays instead","A storm brings many outage calls: PAUSE, and a declared emergency's price limits","At the counter: a lamp that can't be fixed safely, a light still wired in, or a drop-off nobody picks up"]}

more: A downed or sparking power line: stay at least 30 feet away, keep others away, and call the power company. Call 911 if anyone is hurt.
A booking can come later, once the fire department or the power company says it's safe.

ops.does: Say half of Alex's home loses power at 6:40pm. The plug-in marks it urgent, and Sam has an electrician on call tonight. So the AI offers to send someone now, with an arrival estimate, not a window.
more: After hours, the service call is $149, not $89. It's held the same way, not taken, and comes off the repair.
Flat-price jobs cost $60 more after hours. Alex sees the after-hours price before booking.
The electrician on call takes it once Alex books. If nobody does, anything held is released, and Alex is told.
Sam set who's on call with his team: open hours too, plus nights, weekends and holidays, with a backup.
Nobody on call right now: the soonest times show first, as for work that's never sent now.
Sparks, smoke or a burning smell is never sent now. It gets the 911 message first.
Where the state's rules limit prices in a declared emergency, those limits apply.
